label: Bianca Modenese

about.text: An Italian dual-purpose cattle breed from the province of Modena in Emilia-Romagna, with its major emphasis on milk. Its milk is suited to cheese-making, and in the past it was widely used for Parmigiano Reggiano. Its numbers have fallen from about 120,000 cows around 1940 to about 650 today.

sources.text: Province of Modena, cheese-making and Parmigiano Reggiano use from the Wikipedia article (fetched). Dual-purpose aptitude with major emphasis on milk, the population peak around 1940 and the 'today approximately 650 cows' figure from the Regional Cattle Breeds page (fetched). The 650 figure has no stated year.

Wikipedia: 'first documented in the mid-19th century and was officially called Modenese from 1880'; origin unknown, possibly from Reggiana and Podolica stock. The Regional Cattle Breeds page says the breed descends from the reddish cattle of the Carpi area. Formed range is therefore 1850 (the mid-19th century, read as about 1850) to 1880.
'2012: 1,022 total reported (FAO Domestic Animal Diversity Information System, DAD-IS)', as cited in the Wikipedia article. DAD-IS itself was not opened.
'4,700 in 305 days of lactation; with 3.3% fat and 3.4% protein' (Regional Cattle Breeds, fetched). The same figures are given in the Wikipedia article, citing the EuReCa project.
'4,700 in 305 days of lactation' (Regional Cattle Breeds, fetched); the Wikipedia article gives the same figure, citing the EuReCa project. No year or recording country is stated.
'Double purpose, with major emphasis on milk' (fetched). Milk ranked first as the main purpose.

Listed as 'endangered-maintained' in 2007 (Rischkowsky & Pilling, Global Databank annex), as cited in the Wikipedia article. The same status is recorded for 1995 and 2000. DAD-IS itself was not opened, so this is the citing article's record of DAD-IS.

facts.v: Some Parmigiano Reggiano is now made using only Bianca Modenese milk.

sources.text: 'In the 21st century, some Parmigiano Reggiano is made using only Bianca Modenese milk (EuReCa Project)', as stated in the Wikipedia article.

facts.v: About 120,000 cows at the peak around 1940, a minimum of 300 cows in 2000, and about 650 today.

sources.text: 'The population reached a maximum of about 120,000 cows around 1940', 'In 2000: a minimum of 300 cows', 'Today approximately 650 cows' (fetched).

gaps: The DAD-IS page itself was not opened; the 1,022 head count and the 2007 risk status are as cited by Wikipedia. The 650 cows figure has no year. The 2005 count (about 800 head, 258 in the herd book) is in the Wikipedia article but was not used. No recording country is given for the yield.
